<!-- version: 2.41.0 -->
The weather card on your dashboard was naming the wrong days. It labelled the first column of the forecast "Today" whatever stood there, and because the running day is already shown above it, that column was in fact tomorrow. The row read as though a day were missing, and every weekday after it was off by one. Each day is now named from its own date instead of its position. The card also shows today's high and low beside the current temperature, which until now it showed for every day except the one you are actually living through. Households still using an older OpenWeatherMap key get a second correction here: their forecast was grouped by UTC days rather than the days at the weather location, which shifted the whole row for anyone living well east or west of the prime meridian.

If your household has set a time zone that differs from the device you are reading on, several parts of the app were quietly answering with the device's clock instead. A task entered for 21:00 could be shown at an entirely different time, and could read as due today while sitting under Tomorrow in the same list. The same clock decided which day the date picker rings, which month Budget and Inventory open on, which medications still count as due today, and the date filled in for a new shared expense. All of them now follow the household time zone.

Nothing needs configuring and nothing changes about your data. If your household has never set a time zone of its own, the app behaves exactly as it did before.

Full release notes are available at https://github.com/ulsklyc/yuvomi/releases/tag/v2.41.0
